issues.legal_issue: The constitutional property guarantee in force when an acquisition law took effect governs the law’s validity if a later constitutional change is not retrospective.
material_facts: The challenged acquisition law came into force before a later constitutional amendment altered the property guarantee.
The later amendment was not given retrospective operation.
issues.conclusion: The law’s validity had to be assessed under the constitutional provisions as they stood when the law came into force.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Article 31 as it stood before the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955, and held that the later amendment, having no retrospective operation, did not govern the validity of the earlier law. It referred to Chiranjit Lal Chowdhuri v. Union of India, State of West Bengal v. Subodh Gopal Bose, and State of West Bengal v. Mrs. Bela Banerjee.

predicates.acquisition_law_validity_challenge: A person challenges the constitutional validity of a law authorising compulsory acquisition of property.
predicates.law_predates_nonretrospective_constituti: The acquisition law took effect before a later constitutional change, and that change was not made retrospective.

issues.definition: When an acquisition law takes effect before a non-retrospective constitutional change, the earlier property guarantee governs the validity challenge.

issues.legal_issue: A law that fixes compensation for compulsory acquisition by reference to a substantially earlier market value, without establishing that the amount remains a just equivalent at acquisition, violates the applicable property guarantee.
material_facts: The acquisition law fixed compensation by reference to the land’s market value on a date many years before acquisition notifications were issued.
The law denied owners increases in land value between that fixed date and the acquisition notifications.

The State presented no material showing that the earlier value gave owners a just monetary equivalent when their interests were acquired or that later appreciation was attributable to a proposed acquisition scheme.
The law took effect before the later constitutional amendment, which was not retrospective.
issues.conclusion: The provision fixing compensation by reference to the earlier market value was invalid under the property guarantee applicable when the law took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 31(2) as it stood before the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955, compensation had to be a just equivalent of the property taken. State of West Bengal v. Mrs. Bela Banerjee held that an arbitrary ceiling based on an anterior value, without reference to value at acquisition, was not due compensation. Although a rise in value attributable to a known acquisition scheme may be disregarded, a principle denying all increments from a fixed date to the acquisition notification is prima facie insufficient; the State must show that the earlier valuation nevertheless provides a just equivalent. The Court also relied on Chiranjit Lal Chowdhuri v. Union of India and State of West Bengal v. Subodh Gopal Bose concerning the constitutional protection against compulsory deprivation of property.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_chal: An owner challenges the compensation basis in a law authorising compulsory acquisition of property.
predicates.earlier_property_guarantee_applies: The acquisition law took effect before a later constitutional change that was not made retrospective.
predicates.compensation_uses_substantially_earlier_: The law fixes compensation by reference to market value on a date substantially before the acquisition notification and denies later increases in value.
predicates.no_evidence_earlier_value_is_just_equiva: The State provides no evidence that the earlier valuation gives the owner a just monetary equivalent at acquisition or that later appreciation resulted from a known acquisition scheme.

issues.definition: If a compensation challenge concerns a law governed by the earlier property guarantee, the law uses a substantially earlier market value, and the State does not establish that value as a just equivalent, the anterior-date compensation rule is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A law that excludes the value of acquired non-agricultural improvements from compensation denies just compensation under the applicable property guarantee.
material_facts: The acquisition included the owner’s interest in the land and things attached to it, including buildings and other structures.
The compensation law excluded the value of non-agricultural improvements made after its specified benchmark date.
The owner could be deprived of those improvements without receiving their value, whether or not the owner could remove them.
The law took effect before the later constitutional amendment, which was not retrospective.
issues.conclusion: The provision excluding the value of non-agricultural improvements from compensation was invalid under the property guarantee applicable when the law took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2), as it stood before the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955, required just indemnification for compulsory acquisition. Section 3(a) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, defined land to include benefits arising from land and things attached to the earth; acquisition therefore included the owner’s interest in buildings and other structures. Excluding their value denied compensation for part of the property taken. The Court relied on the just-equivalent principle in State of West Bengal v. Mrs. Bela Banerjee and the constitutional property principles discussed in Chiranjit Lal Chowdhuri v. Union of India and State of West Bengal v. Subodh Gopal Bose.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_chal: An owner challenges the compensation basis in a law authorising compulsory acquisition of property.
predicates.earlier_property_guarantee_applies: The acquisition law took effect before a later constitutional change that was not made retrospective.
predicates.non_agricultural_improvements_are_acquir: The acquisition takes the owner’s non-agricultural improvements along with the land.
predicates.compensation_excludes_their_value: The compensation calculation omits the value of those improvements, leaving the owner without payment for them.

issues.definition: If a compulsory acquisition takes non-agricultural improvements and the applicable earlier property guarantee governs, excluding those improvements’ value from compensation makes the exclusion invalid.
